# StealthCup: Realistic, Multi-Stage, Evasion-Focused CTF for Benchmarking IDS

  * Manuel Kern (Autor:in und Vortragende:r)
  * , Dominik Steffan

  * , Florian Skopik

  * University of Vienna

Publikation: Beitrag in Buch oder Tagungsband › Vortrag mit Beitrag in Tagungsband › Begutachtung

## Abstract

Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) are critical to defending enterprise and industrial control environments, yet evaluating their effectiveness under realistic conditions remains an open challenge. Existing benchmarks rely on synthetic datasets (e.g., NSL-KDD, CICIDS2017) or scripted replay frameworks, which fail to capture adaptive adversary behavior. Even MITRE ATT&CK Evaluations, while influential, are host-centric and assume malware-driven compromise, thereby under-representing stealthy, multi-stage intrusions across IT and OT domains. We present StealthCup, a novel evaluation methodology that operationalizes IDS benchmarking as an evasion-focused Capture-the-Flag competition. Professional penetration testers engaged in multi-stage attack chains on a realistic IT/OT testbed, with IDS detection penalizing their scores. The event generated structured attacker writeups, validated detections, and PCAPs, host logs, and alerts. Our results reveal that out of 32 exercised attack techniques, 11 were not detected by any IDS configuration. Open-source systems (Wazuh, Suricata) produced high false-positive rates (>90%), while commercial tools generated fewer false positives but also missed more attacks. Comparison with the Volt Typhoon APT advisory confirmed strong realism: all 28 applicable techniques were exercised, 19 appeared in writeups, and 9 in forensic traces. These findings demonstrate that StealthCup elicits attacker behavior closely aligned with state-sponsored TTPs, while exposing blind spots across both open-source and commercial IDS. The resulting datasets and methodology provide a reproducible foundation for future stealth-focused IDS evaluation.

# 🇦🇹 Stealth-Cup

by 0x01DA 🇦🇹 Austria website CTFtime

StealthCup is an evasion focused CTF and a research project by AIT, held this year at Hackfest in Quebec City. Most CTFs reward speed. StealthCup rewards staying invisible.

Teams attack a live IT and OT enterprise range while a real SOC stack watches. The team that reaches its objectives with the fewest severe detections wins. Up to 12 teams compete, each playing an IT part and an OT part, for the overall cup plus separate IT and OT cups. Detections are shown in real time so teams can adapt their evasion strategy. Resets of infrastructure and scores are possible but cost points.

Ideal team size is 4 to 8 players, with 2 to 4 on each side. The event is designed for professionals with a pentesting background, familiarity with evasion techniques, Windows and OT environments is an advantage. The event runs in English. Technical details and objectives are shared with confirmed teams a few days before the event.

Attack paths and evasion tricks from the event feed into detection research. The 2025 results were published at ACM AsiaCCS 2026. Winners join the StealthCup Hall of Fame and are published on the website, participants can opt for anonymity.

Registration: team registration at https://stealth.ait.ac.at/team-application/, individuals without a team at https://stealth.ait.ac.at/individual-registration/

StealthCup 2026 went to Canada 🇦🇹🇨🇦 After months of building the range in Vienna, we ran it live at Hackfest in Québec City, with teams competing on-site and remotely. The challenge: attack a live IT and OT range while a real SOC stack watches. The quietest team wins. Speed alone won’t win this one! 😏 12 teams tried to break into our haunted plant on Halloween. Two of us travelled to Canada to run the event, with support from our colleagues back home. HarfangLab, Suricata and Wazuh were watching, and the range had 2 TB of RAM behind it. Our sensors had plenty to do: - 99.9 million events captured - 71,489 alerts raised - 492 attacker sessions recorded At one point, the alarm storm hit 19,529 alerts in five minutes. A fairly loud Halloween for a competition called StealthCup. 👻 One unexpected highlight: The weird indoor swimming pool at the Hackfest hotel, with little balconies facing it. After 48 hours of setting up and running the infrastructure, we finally got to use it. Very much needed. 😅 Then there was handing over the prizes to people who had travelled a long way to compete, and the Hackfest crew making us feel right at home in Québec. There’s a research side to all of this, too. Every run becomes a labeled detection dataset. Our results from StealthCup 2025 were published at ACM AsiaCCS 2026. Huge congratulations to m1kulov3rz (Max Günther), p4wxiπ, PetitdodoXEmilio (Ashiahanim Ayassor, Émilio Gonzalez), InsecureByDesign (Ahmed Houssem BOUALEM)! A big thank you to Felix Schuster, Dominik Steffan, Patrick Himler and Florian Skopik for building and running this with me, and to Patrick Mathieu and the whole Hackfest crew for hosting us. Thanks to AIT Austrian Institute of Technology, Hackfest, CyberSecurityAustria CSA, IKARUS Security GmbH and HarfangLab for making it happen. And a special thank you to Lisa Kern for keeping us supplied with food and coffee when we needed it most. #StealthCup #Hackfest #OTSecurity #CTF

# StealthCup 2025: Evasion-Focused IDS Benchmarking

StealthCup is a novel evaluation framework that benchmarks Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) under realistic, adversarial conditions.
Instead of replaying synthetic datasets, StealthCup uses evasion-focused Capture-the-Flag (CTF) challenges executed by professional penetration testers on a validated IT/OT testbed.

The project combines:

  * A fully automated, reproducible Infrastructure-as-Code setup (Terraform, Ansible, Packer) spanning enterprise IT (Active Directory, Windows/Linux servers) and OT environments (virtualized PLCs, SCADA, historians).
  * Realistic, multi-stage attack chains (IT → OT pivoting, AD takeover, PLC manipulation).
  * A fully automated, reproducible Infrastructure-as-Code setup (Terraform, Ansible, Packer) spanning enterprise IT and OT environments.
  * Comparative evaluation of open-source (Suricata, Wazuh) and anonymized commercial IDS solutions.
  * Open datasets of alerts, PCAPs, logs, and structured attacker writeups.

StealthCup complements traditional benchmarks by exposing where IDS configurations fail against stealthy adversaries.

## Key Documents

  * Event Rules of the Game (PDF) – CTF competition format and scoring.
  * Attack Walkthrough (MD) – Step-by-step multi-stage intrusion example (for others see the writeups)
  * Writeups
  * Attack Chains (MD) – Overview of the implemented TTPs.
  * Plumetech Story (PDF) – Narrative background used during the event.

### Scientific Application & Results

  * Evaluation CSV
  * IDS FP Labeling
  * Comparison with Volt Typhoon TTPs (XLSX)
  * StealthCup Event Timeline (XLSX)

### IDS Configuration & Detection

  * Wazuh Detection Blog - Detecting State of the Art Active Directory attacks
  * Local Wazuh Rules
  * Custom Suricata Rules

## Infrastructure

The `provisioning/` directories contain Terraform, Ansible, and Packer configurations for deploying the full IT/OT environment.
Scripts and utilities for redeployment, testing, and simulation can be found under `scripts/` and `testing/`.
